In [51]:






from Functions.run_epochs_17 import *

#--------------------- Take current protocol details -----------------------
ACTIVE_PROTOCOL = 2
pcfg = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[ACTIVE_PROTOCOL]
BEST_CKPT = pcfg['ckpt']                      # protocol-specific checkpoint (Path to save best model checkpoint)
result_dir = pcfg['result']                   # protocol-specific result
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# -------------------- Training History Storage --------------------
# Create a dictionary of empty lists to record metrics for every epoch—losses, ACER, AUC (for both train and val), 
# the loss components, and the learning rate. 
# Append these in each epoch, so the training curve can be analysed later.
history = {
    'train_loss':[], 'dev_loss':[],                  # total loss per epoch (train/val)
    'train_acer':[], 'dev_acer':[],                  # ACER metric per epoch (train/val)
    'train_bpcer':[], 'dev_bpcer':[],                # BPCER metric per epoch (train/val)
    'dev_apcer':[],                                  # 
    'train_auc': [], 'dev_auc': [],                  # AUC metric per epoch (train/val)
    'focal':[],      'supcon':[],                    # loss component tracking (train only)
    'dev_focal':[], 'dev_supcon':[],
    'lr': []                                         # learning rate per epoch
}

# -------------------- Early Stopping Setup --------------------
# Track the best validation ACER so far. Starts at infinity (so the first epoch always counts as an improvement). 
# Lower ACER = better.
best_dev_acer = float('inf')
# Counts how many epochs have passed without improvement
patience_counter = 0
# If validation doesn't improve for 7 epochs in a row, stop training (early stopping)
PATIENCE = 7


# Start Training time
train_start_time = time.time()   # record start

# -------------------- Training Start Info --------------------
# Print a startup message
print(f'Training for {CFG.N_EPOCHS} epochs | Patience={PATIENCE}')
print('='*80)

# -------------------- Main Training Loop --------------------
# Loop over all epochs
for epoch in range(CFG.N_EPOCHS):
    # Update the learning rate for this epoch (warmup/cosine). Returns the LR(s)
    current_lr = scheduler.step(epoch)

    # -------------------- Training Phase --------------------
    # Training pass: run a full epoch of training. Gets back the average loss, metrics, and loss components. 
    # (The three _ ignore the returned probs/labels/attack types)
    train_loss, train_metrics, _, _, train_comps, _ = run_epoch(
        model, train_loader_P2, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler, is_train=True, epoch=epoch)

    # -------------------- Validation Phase --------------------
    # Validation pass: run the validation data (no weight updates, scaler=None, is_train=False)
    dev_loss, dev_metrics, _, _, dev_comps, _ = run_epoch(
        model, dev_loader_P2, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False, epoch=epoch)

    # -------------------- Store Metrics in History --------------------
    # Record this epoch's losses and metrics into the history.
    history['train_loss'].append(train_loss)
    history['dev_loss'].append(dev_loss)
    history['train_acer'].append(train_metrics['ACER'])
    history['dev_acer'].append(dev_metrics['ACER'])
    history['train_auc'].append(train_metrics['AUC'])
    history['dev_auc'].append(dev_metrics['AUC'])
    history['train_bpcer'].append(train_metrics['BPCER'])
    history['dev_bpcer'].append(dev_metrics['BPCER'])
    history['dev_apcer'].append(dev_metrics['APCER'])
    history['dev_focal'].append(dev_comps['focal'])
    history['dev_supcon'].append(dev_comps['supcon'])

    # store loss components (training only)
    history['focal'].append(train_comps['focal'])
    history['supcon'].append(train_comps['supcon'])

    # store learning rate (use the full-rate group for a clean single value)
    history['lr'].append(current_lr[-1] if isinstance(current_lr, (list, tuple)) else current_lr)

    # -------------------- Model Improvement Check --------------------
    # Check if this epoch's validation ACER beat the best so far. If yes, mark it with a "BEST" star in the log.
    improved = dev_metrics['ACER'] < best_dev_acer
    star = ' * BEST' if improved else ''

    # -------------------- Logging --------------------
    # Print a summary line for this epoch:
    # losses, ACER, AUC, loss components, and the BEST marker.
    print(f"Ep {epoch+1:02d}/{CFG.N_EPOCHS} | "
          f"Loss T:{train_loss:.4f} V:{dev_loss:.4f} | "
          f"ACER T:{train_metrics['ACER']:.4f} V:{dev_metrics['ACER']:.4f} | "
          f"AUC:{dev_metrics['AUC']:.4f} | "
          f"[focal={train_comps['focal']:.3f} supcon={train_comps['supcon']:.3f}]"
          f"{star}")

    # -------------------- Save Best Model --------------------
    # If improved: update the best score, reset patience, and save the model checkpoint to disk.
    if improved:
        # update best score
        best_dev_acer = dev_metrics['ACER']
        # reset patience counter
        patience_counter = 0
        # save model checkpoint
        torch.save({
            'epoch': epoch+1,
            'state_dict': model.state_dict(),
            'optimizer_state_dict': optimizer.state_dict(),   # for resuming
            'scaler_state_dict': scaler.state_dict(),         # for resuming (mixed precision)
            'dev_acer': best_dev_acer,
            'dev_metrics': dev_metrics,
            'history': history,                               # training curves
        }, BEST_CKPT)
    
    # If not improved: increment the patience counter. If it hits 7, stop training early
    else:
        # no improvement --> increase patience counter
        patience_counter += 1
        # -------------------- Early Stopping Condition --------------------
        if patience_counter >= PATIENCE:
            print(f'\nEarly stopping at epoch {epoch+1}')
            break

# -------------------- Training Finished --------------------
print(f'\nTraining complete. Best dev ACER: {best_dev_acer:.4f}')

# Print total training time
# Compute total elapsed time
elapsed = time.time() - train_start_time
hours, rem = divmod(int(elapsed), 3600)
minutes, seconds = divmod(rem, 60)
print(f'Total training time = {hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{seconds:02d}')

def plot_training_history(history):
    # X-axis values = epoch numbers (1, 2, 3, ...)
    epochs = range(1, len(history['train_loss']) + 1)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(18, 14))
    fig.suptitle('Training History — Baseline Multi-Stream PAD Model',
                 fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

    # ---- [0,0] Total Loss (train vs val) ----
    axes[0, 0].plot(epochs, history['train_loss'], 'b-o', ms=3, label='Train')
    axes[0, 0].plot(epochs, history['dev_loss'],   'r-o', ms=3, label='Dev/Val')
    axes[0, 0].set_title('Total Loss')
    axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Loss')
    axes[0, 0].legend(); axes[0, 0].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [0,1] ACER % (train vs val) ----
    axes[0, 1].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['train_acer']], 'b-o', ms=3, label='Train')
    axes[0, 1].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['dev_acer']],   'r-o', ms=3, label='Dev/Val')
    axes[0, 1].set_title('ACER % (lower=better)')
    axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('ACER (%)')
    axes[0, 1].legend(); axes[0, 1].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [0,2] BPCER % (train vs val) ----
    axes[0, 2].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['train_bpcer']], 'b-o', ms=3, label='Train')
    axes[0, 2].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['dev_bpcer']],   'r-o', ms=3, label='Dev/Val')
    axes[0, 2].set_title('BPCER % (lower=better)')
    axes[0, 2].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[0, 2].set_ylabel('BPCER (%)')
    axes[0, 2].legend(); axes[0, 2].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [1,0] APCER vs BPCER % (validation) ----
    axes[1, 0].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['dev_apcer']], 'g-o', ms=3, label='APCER (Dev/Val)')
    axes[1, 0].plot(epochs, [a*100 for a in history['dev_bpcer']], 'm-o', ms=3, label='BPCER (Dev/Val)')
    axes[1, 0].set_title('APCER vs BPCER on Validation (lower=better)')
    axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Error rate (%)')
    axes[1, 0].legend(); axes[1, 0].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [1,1] ROC-AUC (train vs val) ----
    axes[1, 1].plot(epochs, history['train_auc'], 'b-o', ms=3, label='Train')
    axes[1, 1].plot(epochs, history['dev_auc'],   'r-o', ms=3, label='Dev/Val')
    axes[1, 1].set_title('ROC-AUC (higher=better)')
    axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('ROC-AUC')
    axes[1, 1].set_ylim([0.5, 1.01])
    axes[1, 1].legend(); axes[1, 1].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [1,2] Loss Components: Training ----
    axes[1, 2].plot(epochs, history['focal'],  'b-', lw=2, label='Focal')
    axes[1, 2].plot(epochs, history['supcon'], 'r-', lw=2, label='SupCon')
    axes[1, 2].set_title('Loss Components: Training')
    axes[1, 2].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[1, 2].set_ylabel('Component Loss')
    axes[1, 2].legend(); axes[1, 2].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [2,0] Loss Components: Validation ----
    axes[2, 0].plot(epochs, history['dev_focal'],  'b-', lw=2, label='Focal')
    axes[2, 0].plot(epochs, history['dev_supcon'], 'r-', lw=2, label='SupCon')
    axes[2, 0].set_title('Loss Components: Validation')
    axes[2, 0].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[2, 0].set_ylabel('Component Loss')
    axes[2, 0].legend(); axes[2, 0].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [2,1] Learning Rate (log scale) ----

    axes[2, 1].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[2, 1].set_ylabel('Learning Rate (log scale)')
    axes[2, 1].set_yscale('log')
    axes[2, 1].grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- [2,2] Summary text box (no axes) ----
    axes[2, 2].axis('off')

    text += f"Best Val AUC:  {max(history['dev_auc']):.4f}\n"
    text += f"Epochs trained: {len(epochs)}"
    axes[2, 2].text(0.1, 0.5, text, transform=axes[2, 2].transAxes,
                    fontsize=14, verticalalignment='center')

    plt.tight_layout()
    result_dir = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[2]['result']
    plt.savefig(result_dir / 'training_history_protocol_2.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()

Protocol 2 - Load best model and evaluate on test set¶


















In [53]:






# =================== Load best model and evaluate on the TEST set ===================================================
# Loads the best checkpoint saved during training, runs ONE pass over the test
# set (unseen data), then finds the decision threshold that minimises ACER and
# reports the final metrics at that threshold.

# --- 1. Load the best checkpoint (if it exists) -------------------------------
if BEST_CKPT.exists():
    # Read the checkpoint file onto the current device
    ckpt = torch.load(BEST_CKPT, map_location=DEVICE, weights_only=False)
    # Restore the model's trained weights
    model.load_state_dict(ckpt['state_dict'])
    # The print confirms which epoch's model loaded.
    print(f'Loaded best checkpoint (epoch {ckpt["epoch"]}, val ACER={ckpt["dev_acer"]:.4f})')
else:
    # No checkpoint -> warn, but still evaluate whatever is currently in `model`
    print('[WARNING] No best checkpoint found; evaluating current in-memory model.')

# --- 2. Run one evaluation pass over the validation set -----------------------------
# is_train=False -> no weight updates, no gradients (pure evaluation).
# scaler=None    -> plain FP32 inference.
# take the loss, metrics, the predicted probabilities (val_probs) and (val_labels); 
# ignore the loss-component dict (using _)
# Take the attacks types for further anyalysis later
dev_loss, dev_metrics, dev_probs, dev_labels, _, _ = run_epoch(
    model, dev_loader_P2, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)


# --- 3. Find the threshold that minimises ACER --------------------------------
# The model outputs probabilities (0–1), but we need a cut-off to decide real vs. fake. 
# Instead of assuming 0.5, this step tries 100 thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9, computes ACER at each, 
# and picks the one with the lowest ACER (np.argmin finds the index of the minimum). 
# This finds the optimal decision boundary for the model.
dev_labels_int = dev_labels.round().astype(int)                                                 # ensure integer labels
thresholds = np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, 100)                                                         # 100 candidate cut-offs
dev_acers = [compute_pad_metrics(dev_labels_int, dev_probs, t)['ACER'] for t in thresholds]
best_thresh = thresholds[np.argmin(dev_acers)]                                                  # threshold with lowest ACER

# --- 4. Compute final metrics at the chosen threshold -------------------------
# Run test pass
test_loss, test_metrics, test_probs, test_labels, _, test_attacks = run_epoch(
    model, test_loader_P2, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)
test_labels_int = test_labels.round().astype(int)
opt_metrics = compute_pad_metrics(test_labels_int, test_probs, threshold=best_thresh)

# --- 5. Report ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Print each metric as a percentage, labeled with whether higher or lower is better
print(f'\nOptimal Threshold = {best_thresh:.3f}')
print('=' * 50)
for k, v in opt_metrics.items():
    # Label each metric with its "good" direction for readability
    direction = 'lower=better' if k in ['APCER', 'BPCER', 'ACER'] else 'higher=better'
    print(f'  {k:8s}: {v*100:.2f}%  ({direction})')


# --- 6. Save results to the protocol's result folder ---
result_dir = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[2]['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Save the metrics as JSON
results_to_save = {
    'protocol': 2,
    'best_threshold': float(best_thresh),
    'test_metrics': {k: float(v) for k, v in opt_metrics.items()},
    'checkpoint_epoch': int(ckpt['epoch']) if BEST_CKPT.exists() else None,
}
with open(result_dir / 'test_metrics.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(results_to_save, f, indent=2)

print(f'\nResults saved to {result_dir / "test_metrics.json"}')

Protocol 2 - Per attack result: APCER/ACER/TDR@1%, along with shared BPCER:¶


















In [54]:






# ============================================================================
#  PROTOCOL II — Per-Attack ACER + TDR table (paper format)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  It reuses the test predictions produced there: 
#  test_probs / test_labels / test_attacks / best_thresh. 
#  Also needs compute_tdr_at_fdr() and the (fixed) metric defs.
#
#  Why ACER is computed this way:
#    ACER needs APCER (a SPOOF error) and BPCER (a REAL error). But "real"
#    faces are not attack-specific, so there is no per-attack BPCER. Following
#    the paper, each attack's ACER pairs THAT attack's APCER with the ONE
#    shared overall BPCER:  per-attack ACER = (attack APCER + overall BPCER)/2
# ============================================================================

# ---- Pull predictions into plain arrays (aligned per test sample) ----------
probs   = np.asarray(test_probs)                       # spoof probability, 0..1
labels  = np.asarray(test_labels).round().astype(int)  # ground truth: 0=real, 1=spoof
attacks = np.asarray(test_attacks)                     # attack-type string per sample
preds   = (probs >= best_thresh).astype(int)           # hard decision at the chosen threshold

# Strings that mean "real / bona-fide" in the attack_type column
REAL_NAMES = {'real', 'live', 'Real', 'Live'}

# ---- Split every sample into real vs spoof --------------------------------
# A sample is "real" if its attack_type says so OR its label is 0 (belt & braces).
is_real    = np.isin(attacks, list(REAL_NAMES)) | (labels == 0)
real_mask  = is_real
spoof_mask = ~is_real

# ---- Overall BPCER (shared by every attack) -------------------------------
# BPCER = real faces wrongly rejected as spoof  /  total real faces.
# This is computed ONCE and reused in every attack's ACER.
n_real        = real_mask.sum()
real_rejected = ((preds == 1) & real_mask).sum()       # real predicted as spoof
overall_bpcer = real_rejected / (n_real + 1e-8)        # 1e-8 guards divide-by-zero

# All real faces' probs/labels — reused for each attack's TDR computation
real_probs  = probs[real_mask]
real_labels = labels[real_mask]                        # all zeros

# ---- Per-attack metrics ----------------------------------------------------
rows = []
spoof_attack_names = sorted(set(attacks[spoof_mask].tolist()))   # the 14 attack types

for atk in spoof_attack_names:
    # Mask selecting only THIS attack's spoof samples
    m = (attacks == atk) & spoof_mask
    n_atk = m.sum()
    if n_atk == 0:
        continue                                       # skip attacks with no samples

    # APCER for this attack = its spoofs that slipped through (predicted real)
    #                         / its total spoofs
    atk_passed = ((preds == 0) & m).sum()              # this attack's spoofs called "real"
    atk_apcer  = atk_passed / (n_atk + 1e-8)

    # Per-attack ACER = (this attack's APCER + the shared overall BPCER) / 2
    atk_acer = (atk_apcer + overall_bpcer) / 2

    # Per-attack TDR@FDR=1%: evaluate this attack's spoofs against ALL real faces
    # (a 2-class problem: reals=0, this-attack=1), at a 1% false-alarm budget.
    combo_probs  = np.concatenate([real_probs,  probs[m]])
    combo_labels = np.concatenate([real_labels, labels[m]])
    atk_tdr = compute_tdr_at_fdr(combo_labels, combo_probs, target_fdr=0.01)

    rows.append({'attack': atk, 'n': int(n_atk),
                 'APCER': atk_apcer * 100, 'ACER': atk_acer * 100, 'TDR': atk_tdr})

# ---- Overall row (all spoofs pooled together) -----------------------------
overall_apcer = ((preds == 0) & spoof_mask).sum() / (spoof_mask.sum() + 1e-8)
overall_acer  = (overall_apcer + overall_bpcer) / 2
overall_tdr   = compute_tdr_at_fdr(labels, probs, target_fdr=0.01)   # all real + all spoof

# ---- Print the table -------------------------------------------------------
print(f"{'Attack':<24}{'n':>5}{'APCER%':>9}{'ACER%':>9}{'TDR@1%':>9}")
print('-' * 56)
for r in rows:

      f"{overall_acer*100:>9.2f}{overall_tdr:>9.2f}")
# BPCER is the same for every attack, so print it once at the bottom
print(f"\nShared overall BPCER (real rejected): {overall_bpcer*100:.2f}%")

# ---- Save for the final paper-format comparison table ----------------------
protocol1_per_attack = {
    'per_attack': rows,
    'overall': {'APCER': overall_apcer * 100, 'BPCER': overall_bpcer * 100,
                'ACER': overall_acer * 100, 'TDR': overall_tdr},
}

# Get the protocol-specific results folder
result_dir = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[2]['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# ---- Save the structured data as JSON ----
with open(result_dir / 'per_attack_result_metrics_protocol_2.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(protocol1_per_attack, f, indent=2)

# ============== ROC + Confusion Matrix =================================================
# Two diagnostic plots side by side from the TEST predictions:
#   Left  : ROC curve (TPR vs FPR across thresholds) with the AUC score.
#   Right : Confusion matrix at the chosen threshold (counts + row-%).
# Requires: from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve, roc_auc_score, confusion_matrix

# Make sure the protocol result folder exists
result_dir = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[2]['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Create a 1-row, 2-column figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# ----- Left panel: ROC curve -------------------------------------------------
# roc_curve returns the false-positive rate, true-positive rate, and the
# thresholds it swept (we ignore the thresholds with '_').
fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(test_labels.round().astype(int), test_probs)
# Area under the ROC curve (1.0 = perfect, 0.5 = random)
auc_score = roc_auc_score(test_labels.round().astype(int), test_probs)
# Plot the ROC curve
axes[0].plot(fpr, tpr, 'b-', lw=2, label=f'ROC (AUC={auc_score:.4f})')
# Diagonal reference line = random-guess baseline
axes[0].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', alpha=0.5)
axes[0].legend(); axes[0].grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_title('ROC Curve: Test Data')
axes[0].set_xlabel('FPR (BPCER)')      # x-axis: false positive rate
axes[0].set_ylabel('TPR')              # y-axis: true positive rate

# ----- Right panel: Confusion matrix -----------------------------------------
# Turn probabilities into hard 0/1 predictions using the chosen threshold
y_pred = (test_probs >= best_thresh).astype(int)
# Raw confusion-matrix counts (rows = true class, cols = predicted class)
cm = confusion_matrix(test_labels.round().astype(int), y_pred)
# Convert each ROW to percentages (so each true class sums to 100%)
cm_pct = cm.astype(float) / cm.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) * 100
# Draw the matrix as a heatmap (0–100% colour scale)
im = axes[1].imshow(cm_pct, cmap='Blues', vmin=0, vmax=100)
plt.colorbar(im, ax=axes[1])
# Label the axes with class names (0=Real, 1=Fake)
axes[1].set_xticks([0, 1]); axes[1].set_xticklabels(['Real', 'Fake'])
axes[1].set_yticks([0, 1]); axes[1].set_yticklabels(['Real', 'Fake'])
# Write the count + percentage inside each cell
for i in range(2):
    for j in range(2):
        axes[1].text(
            j, i, f'{cm[i,j]:,}\n({cm_pct[i,j]:.1f}%)',
            ha='center', va='center',
            # white text on dark cells, black on light cells, for readability
            color='white' if cm_pct[i, j] > 50 else 'black',
            fontsize=11
        )
axes[1].set_title(f'Confusion Matrix - Protocol 2 (threshold={best_thresh:.2f})')

# Lay out, save, and display
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(result_dir / 'roc_confusion_protocol_2.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()










































































Protocol 2 - Per-attack-type misclassification bar chart (TEST set)¶


















In [56]:






# ------------- Per-attack-type misclassification bar chart (TEST set) ------------------------------
# Each SPOOF attack type -> % of that type misclassified as REAL (spoof passed through).
# REAL (bona-fide) -> % of real faces misclassified as FAKE -> shown as a SEPARATE
# bar at the END in a different colour.
#
# Requires (aligned per test sample):
#   test_probs, test_labels (0=real, 1=fake), test_attacks, best_thresh
#
# How "real" is identified: any attack-type string in REAL_NAMES is treated as the
# bona-fide/real class. Adjust REAL_NAMES to match your dataset's label for real
# (commonly 'Live', 'Real', or 'live').


# --- which attack-type string(s) mean "real" ---
REAL_NAMES = {'Live', 'Real', 'live', 'real', 'genuine', 'bonafide', 'Bona-fide'}

probs   = np.asarray(test_probs)
labels  = np.asarray(test_labels).round().astype(int)
attacks = np.asarray(test_attacks)
preds   = (probs >= best_thresh).astype(int)

spoof_names, spoof_errs = [], []
real_err, real_name = None, 'Real'

for atk in sorted(set(attacks.tolist())):
    m = attacks == atk
    atk_preds = preds[m]

    # Decide real vs spoof primarily by the name; fall back to label majority.
    is_real = (atk in REAL_NAMES) or (labels[m].mean() < 0.5)

    if is_real:
        # % of real faces wrongly called FAKE (predicted 1)
        real_err  = float(np.mean(atk_preds == 1) * 100)
        real_name = atk
    else:
        # % of this spoof type wrongly called REAL (predicted 0) -> passed through
        spoof_names.append(atk)
        spoof_errs.append(float(np.mean(atk_preds == 0) * 100))

# Spoof bars first, then the Real bar last
names  = spoof_names + ([real_name] if real_err is not None else [])
errs   = spoof_errs  + ([real_err]  if real_err is not None else [])
colors = ['#e76f51'] * len(spoof_names) + (['#2a9d8f'] if real_err is not None else [])

# ----- Plot -----
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
bars = plt.bar(names, errs, color=colors)
plt.ylabel('Wrongly classified (%)')
plt.title(f'Per-Attack Misclassification on Test Set - Protocol 2 (threshold={best_thresh:.2f})\n'
          'red = spoof passed as real   |   green = real rejected as fake')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
for b, e in zip(bars, errs):
    plt.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width()/2, b.get_height(),
             f'{e:.1f}%', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# ----- Print the numbers -----
print(f"{'Category':<22}{'Wrong %':>10}")
print('=' * 34)
for nm, e in zip(names, errs):
    tag = '(real rejected)' if nm == real_name else '(spoof passed)'
    print(f'{nm:<22}{e:>10.2f}   {tag}')

#---- Save results ----
result_dir = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[2]['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
plt.savefig(result_dir / 'per_attack_barchart_protocol_2.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')

# ============================================================================
#  PROTOCOL 3  —  Leave One Camera Out (LOCO)   [OULU-NPU]
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Six camera folds. For each fold i (1..6): Train_i / Dev_i / Test_i hold the
#  videos for that fold's train / validation / test. A separate model is trained
#  per fold and results are averaged (mean +/- std) across the 6 folds.
#
#  This cell only BUILDS and VERIFIES the six folds (no training). Each fold's
#  train / dev / test dataframes are stored in lists for the training loop.
# ============================================================================
from Functions.config import *

# --- 1. Reader for the official partition files -----------------------------
#     OULU-NPU lines are "label,video_name" (e.g. "+1,4_1_11_4"); take the part
#     after the comma. set() de-duplicates any repeated names.
def _read_ids(p):
    ids = set()
    with open(p) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            if ',' in line:
                name = line.split(',')[1].strip()   # video name after the label
            else:
                name = line
            ids.add(name)
    return ids

pc = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[3]

# --- 2. Build + verify the six folds ----------------------------------------
train_dfs_P3 = []   # 6 train dataframes  (index 0 -> Fold 1, ... , index 5 -> Fold 6)
dev_dfs_P3   = []   # 6 dev/val dataframes
test_dfs_P3  = []   # 6 test dataframes

for fold in range(6):                                  # list index 0..5 (Fold 1..6)
    position = fold + 1                                     # human-readable fold/position number

    # Read this fold's three partition files
    train_ids = _read_ids(pc['train_P3'][fold])
    dev_ids   = _read_ids(pc['dev_P3'][fold])
    test_ids  = _read_ids(pc['test_P3'][fold])

    # Select the matching videos from df
    train_df = df[df['subject_id'].isin(train_ids)].copy()
    dev_df   = df[df['subject_id'].isin(dev_ids)].copy()
    test_df  = df[df['subject_id'].isin(test_ids)].copy()

    # Store for the training loop
    train_dfs_P3.append(train_df)
    dev_dfs_P3.append(dev_df)
    test_dfs_P3.append(test_df)

    # ---- Match check (this fold) ----
    print(f'\nMatch check (Fold {position}):')
    print(f'  Total no of train-files in the protocol = {len(train_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(train_df):>5}')
    print(f'  Total no of dev-files in the protocol = {len(dev_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(dev_df):>5}')
    print(f'  Total no of test-files in the protocol = {len(test_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(test_df):>5}')

    # Warn if any split matched nothing
    if len(train_df) == 0 or len(dev_df) == 0 or len(test_df) == 0:
        print('  !! WARNING: 0 matched — the split-file names do not match df["subject_id"].')
        print('     Example df stems:', df['subject_id'].head(3).tolist())
        print('     Example file ids :', list(train_ids)[:3])

    # ---- Totals ----
    print(f'\nFold {position}  ->  Train: {len(train_df):,} | Val: {len(dev_df):,} | Test: {len(test_df):,}')

    # ---- Per-class counts ----
    print(f'\nFold {position} Per-class counts:')
    for name, d in [('Train', train_df), ('Dev/Val', dev_df), ('Test', test_df)]:
        n_real = (d['label'] == 0).sum()
        n_fake = (d['label'] == 1).sum()
        print(f'  {name:<5}: real {n_real:>4} | fake {n_fake:>4}')

    print()   # blank line between folds

# CHECK 1 (Protocol 3) — Subject disjointness across train / dev / test
#                        for ALL 6 camera folds
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Goal: confirm NO subject appears in more than one split within each fold.
# ============================================================================

for fold in range(6):                          # list index 0..5  (Fold 1..6)
    position = fold + 1

    # Per-fold dataframes (from the split cell's lists), named for clarity
    train_df_P3_F = train_dfs_P3[fold]
    dev_df_P3_F   = dev_dfs_P3[fold]
    test_df_P3_F  = test_dfs_P3[fold]

    print('=' * 60)
    print(f'CHECK 1 — Subject disjointness across splits  (Fold {position})')
    print('=' * 60)

    # Unique subject sets per split
    train_subj_P3_F = set(train_df_P3_F['subject_id'])
    dev_subj_P3_F   = set(dev_df_P3_F['subject_id'])
    test_subj_P3_F  = set(test_df_P3_F['subject_id'])

    print(f'Unique subjects -> Train: {len(train_subj_P3_F)} | '
          f'Dev/Val: {len(dev_subj_P3_F)} | Test: {len(test_subj_P3_F)}')

    # Pairwise overlaps (each MUST be empty for no leakage)
    tv = train_subj_P3_F & dev_subj_P3_F
    tt = train_subj_P3_F & test_subj_P3_F
    vt = dev_subj_P3_F   & test_subj_P3_F

    print(f'\nOverlap Train ∩ Dev  : {len(tv)} subjects')
    print(f'Overlap Train ∩ Test : {len(tt)} subjects')
    print(f'Overlap Dev   ∩ Test : {len(vt)} subjects')

    if len(tv) == 0 and len(tt) == 0 and len(vt) == 0:
        print('\nPASS — all three splits are subject-disjoint (no leakage).')
    else:
        print('\nFAIL — subjects shared across splits (LEAKAGE):')
        if tv: print('   Train∩Dev :', list(tv)[:10])
        if tt: print('   Train∩Test:', list(tt)[:10])
        if vt: print('   Dev∩Test  :', list(vt)[:10])

    # Videos vs unique subjects per split (multiple videos per subject is fine)
    print('\nVideos vs unique subjects per split:')
    for name, d in [('Train', train_df_P3_F), ('Dev/Val', dev_df_P3_F), ('Test', test_df_P3_F)]:
        print(f'  {name:<5}: {len(d):>4} videos | {d["subject_id"].nunique():>4} unique subjects')

Protocol 3 - For all the data in Protocol 3, check if the cache files are correctly formed:¶


















In [64]:






# ============================================================================
#  CACHE COVERAGE CHECK (Protocol 3)  —  directories, FFT files, flow files
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Protocol 3 has 6 camera folds, each with its own train/dev/test. Rather than
#  check one split, this gathers EVERY unique video used across all 6 folds
#  (train + dev + test) and verifies three levels of cache completeness:
#     1. the precompute DIRECTORY exists
#     2. all N_FRAMES  freq_*.npy  (FFT) files are present
#     3. all N_FRAMES  flow_*.npy  (optical flow) files are present
#  Any video failing a level triggers the on-the-fly recompute fallback in the
#  dataset (slower, and — for FFT — the source of the CUDA-in-worker crash),
#  so the goal is zero incompletes on every level.
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds (train+dev+test) ------
#     A video can appear in several folds; use a set of paths to check each once.
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P3[fold], dev_dfs_P3[fold], test_dfs_P3[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

missing_dir  = []   # videos with NO precompute folder at all
missing_fft  = []   # videos whose folder exists but freq_*.npy files are incomplete
missing_flow = []   # videos whose folder exists but flow_*.npy files are incomplete

for path in all_paths:
    vid_id  = Path(path).stem
    vid_dir = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id

    # ---- Level 1: does the cache directory exist at all? ----
    if not vid_dir.exists():
        missing_dir.append(vid_id)
        continue                       # no folder -> can't check files inside

    # ---- Level 2: count the FFT (freq) files inside the folder ----
    fft_files = list(vid_dir.glob('freq_*.npy'))
    if len(fft_files) < CFG.N_FRAMES:  # expect one freq file per frame
        missing_fft.append((vid_id, len(fft_files)))

    # ---- Level 3: count the optical-flow files inside the folder ----
    flow_files = list(vid_dir.glob('flow_*.npy'))
    if len(flow_files) < CFG.N_FRAMES: # expect one flow file per frame
        missing_flow.append((vid_id, len(flow_files)))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Report
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
total = len(all_paths)
print(f"Total unique videos (all 6 folds): {total}")
print(f"Missing cache directory          : {len(missing_dir)}")
print(f"Incomplete FFT (freq_*.npy)      : {len(missing_fft)}")
print(f"Incomplete flow (flow_*.npy)     : {len(missing_flow)}")

# Show a few examples for each problem level (only if any exist)
if missing_dir:
    print("\nExamples — missing directory:")
    print("  ", missing_dir[:10])
if missing_fft:
    print("\nExamples — incomplete FFT (vid_id, n_freq_files):")
    print("  ", missing_fft[:10])
if missing_flow:
    print("\nExamples — incomplete flow (vid_id, n_flow_files):")
    print("  ", missing_flow[:10])

# Clean bill of health
if not (missing_dir or missing_fft or missing_flow):
    print("\nAll cache directories, FFT files, and flow files are complete.")

























Total unique videos (all 6 folds): 4871
Missing cache directory          : 0
Incomplete FFT (freq_*.npy)      : 0
Incomplete flow (flow_*.npy)     : 0

All cache directories, FFT files, and flow files are complete.

# ============================================================================
#  USABLE-FRACTION DISTRIBUTION (Protocol 3)  —  all videos across 6 folds
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Reads usable_frac from each video's cached video_meta.json and plots the
#  distribution. Videos below CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC were letterboxed (fallback);
#  the rest were properly aligned. Covers every unique video used across the
#  6 camera folds (train + dev + test).
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds -----------------------
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P3[fold], dev_dfs_P3[fold], test_dfs_P3[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

# --- Build the list of usable_frac values from cached video_meta.json --------
fracs = []
for path in all_paths:
    vid_id = Path(path).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        fracs.append(json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac'])

print(f"Collected usable_frac for {len(fracs)} / {len(all_paths)} videos")

# --- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.hist(fracs, bins=20, color='#534AB7', edgecolor='white')
ax.set_title('Distribution of usable landmark fraction per video (Protocol 3, all folds)',
             fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('usable_frac  (fraction of frames with good landmarks)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of videos', fontsize=11)

# Reference line at the align threshold
ax.axvline(CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC, color='orangered', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Align threshold ({CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC})')

# Region annotations
ax.text(0.97, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.9, 'Aligned\n(high quality)',
        ha='right', color='#1D9E75', fontsize=10)
ax.text(0.03, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.15, 'Letterbox\nfallback',
        ha='left', color='#D85A30', fontsize=10)

ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# --- Quick numeric summary ---------------------------------------------------
import numpy as np
fr = np.array(fracs)
below = (fr < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC).sum()
print(f"Below align threshold ({CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC}): {below} videos "
      f"({below / len(fr) * 100:.2f}%)")
print(f"Min {fr.min():.3f} | Median {np.median(fr):.3f} | Mean {fr.mean():.3f} | Max {fr.max():.3f}")

# ============================================================================
#  LETTERBOX CHECK (Protocol 3)  —  videos below the align threshold
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Collects videos whose usable_frac < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC (i.e. letterboxed
#  fallback), together with their attack types, across all 6 camera folds
#  (train + dev + test, each unique video counted once).
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique (path, label, attack_type) across all 6 folds -------
#     Deduplicate by path so a video shared across folds is checked once.
seen_paths = set()
records = []
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P3[fold], dev_dfs_P3[fold], test_dfs_P3[fold]):
        for _, row in d.iterrows():
            if row['path'] in seen_paths:
                continue
            seen_paths.add(row['path'])
            records.append(row)

# --- Collect videos below the align threshold, WITH their attack types -------
low_videos = []
for row in records:
    vid_id = Path(row['path']).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        uf = json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac']
        if uf < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC:          # < 0.70 -> letterboxed
            low_videos.append({
                'vid_id': vid_id,
                'label': row['label'],
                'attack_type': row.get('attack_type', 'unknown'),
                'usable_frac': round(uf, 3),
            })

print(f"Total letterboxed (usable_frac < {CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC}): {len(low_videos)}\n")

# Percentage of total (unique) videos that were letterboxed
total = len(records)
pct = (len(low_videos) / total * 100) if total else 0.0
print(f"Total unique videos (all 6 folds): {total}")
print(f"Letterboxed %                    : {pct:.6f}%")

# Only print the breakdowns if there ARE letterboxed videos
if low_videos:
    # Count per attack type
    attack_counts = Counter(v['attack_type'] for v in low_videos)
    print("\nLetterboxed videos by attack type:")
    for atk, cnt in attack_counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {atk:30s} : {cnt}")

    # Real vs fake split
    label_counts = Counter(v['label'] for v in low_videos)
    print(f"\nBy label: {dict(label_counts)}")

    # Full list
    print("\nIndividual videos:")
    for v in low_videos:
        print(f"  {v['vid_id']:25s} label={v['label']} attack={v['attack_type']:20s} uf={v['usable_frac']}")
else:
    print("\nNo letterboxed videos — all videos met the alignment threshold.")

# ============================================================================
#  META-FILE DIAGNOSTIC (Protocol 3)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Confirms the letterbox check is actually reading files (not silently finding
#  nothing). Checks two things across all 6 camera folds:
#    (1) how many video_meta.json files were actually found  (key diagnostic)
#    (2) how many of those are letterboxed (usable_frac < threshold)
#  If 'found' is far below the total, the cache path is wrong or precompute is
#  incomplete — and any "0 letterboxed" result would be meaningless.
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds -----------------------
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P3[fold], dev_dfs_P3[fold], test_dfs_P3[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

found = 0
low_videos = []
for path in all_paths:
    vid_id = Path(path).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        found += 1                              # count files actually found
        uf = json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac']
        if uf < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC:
            low_videos.append(vid_id)

print(f"Meta files found: {found} / {len(all_paths)}")   # the key diagnostic
print(f"Letterboxed: {len(low_videos)}")

Protocol 3 - Model Training:¶
    

  • This includes in every loop Train_i/Dev_i/Test_i is trained and evaluated on.¶
    Therefore, every loop has its own datasets split creation, data loaders creation, weighted sampler creation on training data, and optimisation declarations.¶
    • 



















In [39]:






from Functions.run_epochs_17 import *
from Functions.data_pipeline_setup_7 import *
from Functions.weighted_sampler_8 import *
from Functions.full_model_pipeline_13 import *
from Functions.loss_functions_14 import *
from Functions.optimiser_and_scheduler_15 import *

# ============================================================================
#  PROTOCOL 3 — Leave-One-Camera-Out (LOCO)  |  full training + evaluation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Six folds: For each fold a FRESH model is trained on that fold's
#  Train split, validated on its Dev split (threshold tuning + early stopping),
#  and evaluated on its Test split (the held-out camera). Per-fold metrics are
#  collected and later aggregated to mean +/- std across the six folds.
#
#  Everything fold-specific lives INSIDE the loop: datasets, loaders, sampler,
#  fresh model + optimiser + scheduler + scaler, the epoch loop, and the test
#  evaluation. Cross-fold aggregation + plots are done AFTER the loop.
# ============================================================================

ACTIVE_PROTOCOL = 3
pcfg = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[ACTIVE_PROTOCOL]
result_dir = pcfg['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

PATIENCE = 7
protocol3_fold_results = []          # one dict of metrics per fold
overall_start = time.time()

# ============================================================================
#  OUTER LOOP — one model per fold (fold index 0..5 = position 1..6)
# ============================================================================
for fold in range(6):
    position = fold + 1
    print('\n' + '=' * 80)
    print(f'PROTOCOL 3  |  SITUATION(FOLD) {position}  (LOCO configuration {position}: Train_{position}/Dev_{position}/Test_{position})')
    print('=' * 80)

    # ---- Datasets for this fold (OULU paths passed explicitly) -------------
    train_dataset_P3 = PADVideoDataset(
        train_dfs_P3[fold], real_dir=REAL_DIR_OULU, cache_dir=CACHE_DIR_OULU,
        transform=train_transforms, demo_mode=False,
        use_freq=CFG.USE_FREQ_STREAM, use_flow=CFG.USE_FLOW_STREAM)
    dev_dataset_P3 = PADVideoDataset(
        dev_dfs_P3[fold], real_dir=REAL_DIR_OULU, cache_dir=CACHE_DIR_OULU,
        transform=dev_transforms, demo_mode=False,
        use_freq=CFG.USE_FREQ_STREAM, use_flow=CFG.USE_FLOW_STREAM)
    test_dataset_P3 = PADVideoDataset(
        test_dfs_P3[fold], real_dir=REAL_DIR_OULU, cache_dir=CACHE_DIR_OULU,
        transform=dev_transforms, demo_mode=False,
        use_freq=CFG.USE_FREQ_STREAM, use_flow=CFG.USE_FLOW_STREAM)

    # ---- Weighted sampler + loaders ----------------------------------------
    train_sampler_P3 = make_weighted_sampler(train_dataset_P3)
    train_loader_P3 = DataLoader(
        train_dataset_P3, batch_size=CFG.BATCH_SIZE, sampler=train_sampler_P3,
        num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, prefetch_factor=2, persistent_workers=True)
    dev_loader_P3 = DataLoader(
        dev_dataset_P3, batch_size=CFG.BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False,
        num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, prefetch_factor=2, persistent_workers=True)
    test_loader_P3 = DataLoader(
        test_dataset_P3, batch_size=CFG.BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False,
        num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, prefetch_factor=2, persistent_workers=True)

    # ---- Fresh model + loss + optimiser + scheduler + scaler (per fold) -----
    #      Rebuilt every fold so no camera's model carries over. param_groups
    #      reference THIS model's modules, so they are rebuilt here too.
    model = HybridPADModel().to(DEVICE)
    criterion = CompoundFASLoss()
    param_groups = [
        {'params': list(model.cnn_rgb.backbone.parameters()),  'lr': CFG.LR * 0.1, 'name': 'rgb_backbone'},
        {'params': list(model.cnn_rgb.projector.parameters()), 'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'rgb_proj'},
        {'params': list(model.cnn_freq.parameters()),          'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'freq_cnn'},
        {'params': list(model.cnn_flow.parameters()),          'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'flow_cnn'},
        {'params': list(model.stream_gate.parameters()),       'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'gate'},
        {'params': list(model.rnn_encoder.parameters()),       'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'rnn'},
        {'params': list(model.tf_encoder.parameters()),        'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'transformer'},
        {'params': list(model.classifier.parameters()),        'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'classifier'},
        {'params': list(model.proj_head.parameters()),         'lr': CFG.LR,       'name': 'supcon_head'},
    ]
    optimizer = optim.AdamW(param_groups, weight_decay=CFG.WEIGHT_DECAY)
    scheduler = WarmupCosineScheduler(optimizer, CFG.WARMUP_EPOCHS, CFG.N_EPOCHS, CFG.LR)
    scaler    = torch.amp.GradScaler('cuda')

    # ---- Per-fold history + early-stopping state ---------------------------
    history = {
        'train_loss':[], 'dev_loss':[], 'train_acer':[], 'dev_acer':[],
        'train_bpcer':[], 'dev_bpcer':[], 'dev_apcer':[], 'train_auc':[], 'dev_auc':[],
        'focal':[], 'supcon':[], 'dev_focal':[], 'dev_supcon':[], 'lr':[]
    }
    best_dev_acer = float('inf')
    patience_counter = 0
    fold_ckpt = Path(str(pcfg['ckpt_prefix']) + f'fold{position}.pth')   # e.g. ..._fold1.pth

    # ---- Inner training loop (same structure as Protocol 1) ----------------
    for epoch in range(CFG.N_EPOCHS):
        current_lr = scheduler.step(epoch)

        train_loss, train_metrics, _, _, train_comps, _ = run_epoch(
            model, train_loader_P3, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler, is_train=True, epoch=epoch)
        dev_loss, dev_metrics, _, _, dev_comps, _ = run_epoch(
            model, dev_loader_P3, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False, epoch=epoch)

        history['train_loss'].append(train_loss); history['dev_loss'].append(dev_loss)
        history['train_acer'].append(train_metrics['ACER']); history['dev_acer'].append(dev_metrics['ACER'])
        history['train_auc'].append(train_metrics['AUC']);   history['dev_auc'].append(dev_metrics['AUC'])
        history['train_bpcer'].append(train_metrics['BPCER']); history['dev_bpcer'].append(dev_metrics['BPCER'])
        history['dev_apcer'].append(dev_metrics['APCER'])
        history['dev_focal'].append(dev_comps['focal']); history['dev_supcon'].append(dev_comps['supcon'])
        history['focal'].append(train_comps['focal']);   history['supcon'].append(train_comps['supcon'])
        history['lr'].append(current_lr[-1] if isinstance(current_lr, (list, tuple)) else current_lr)

        improved = dev_metrics['ACER'] < best_dev_acer
        star = ' * BEST' if improved else ''
        print(f"  Ep {epoch+1:02d}/{CFG.N_EPOCHS} | "
              f"Loss T:{train_loss:.4f} V:{dev_loss:.4f} | "
              f"ACER T:{train_metrics['ACER']:.4f} V:{dev_metrics['ACER']:.4f} | "
              f"AUC:{dev_metrics['AUC']:.4f}{star}")

        if improved:
            best_dev_acer = dev_metrics['ACER']
            patience_counter = 0
            torch.save({'epoch': epoch+1, 'state_dict': model.state_dict(),
                        'optimizer_state_dict': optimizer.state_dict(),
                        'scaler_state_dict': scaler.state_dict(),
                        'dev_acer': best_dev_acer, 'dev_metrics': dev_metrics,
                        'fold': position, 'history': history}, fold_ckpt)
        else:
            patience_counter += 1
            if patience_counter >= PATIENCE:
                print(f'  Early stopping at epoch {epoch+1}')
                break

    # ---- Evaluate this fold: load best -> tune threshold on Dev -> Test -----
    ckpt = torch.load(fold_ckpt, map_location=DEVICE, weights_only=False)
    model.load_state_dict(ckpt['state_dict'])
    print(f'  Loaded best (epoch {ckpt["epoch"]}, dev ACER={ckpt["dev_acer"]:.4f})')

    # Dev pass -> threshold that minimises ACER
    _, _, dev_probs, dev_labels, _, _ = run_epoch(
        model, dev_loader_P3, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)
    dev_labels_int = dev_labels.round().astype(int)
    thresholds = np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, 100)
    dev_acers = [compute_pad_metrics(dev_labels_int, dev_probs, t)['ACER'] for t in thresholds]
    best_thresh = thresholds[np.argmin(dev_acers)]

    # Test pass -> final metrics at the Dev-tuned threshold
    _, _, test_probs, test_labels, _, _ = run_epoch(
        model, test_loader_P3, optimizer, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)
    test_labels_int = test_labels.round().astype(int)
    m = compute_pad_metrics(test_labels_int, test_probs, threshold=best_thresh)
    tdr = compute_tdr_at_fdr(test_labels_int, test_probs, target_fdr=0.01)

    n_real = int((test_dfs_P3[fold]['label'] == 0).sum())
    n_fake = int((test_dfs_P3[fold]['label'] == 1).sum())

    print(f'  >> Fold {position}: ACER {m["ACER"]*100:.2f}% | APCER {m["APCER"]*100:.2f}% | '
          f'BPCER {m["BPCER"]*100:.2f}% | AUC {m["AUC"]*100:.2f}% | TDR@1% {tdr:.2f}% '
          f'| thr {best_thresh:.3f}  (real {n_real}, fake {n_fake})')

    protocol3_fold_results.append({
        'fold': position, 'ACER': m['ACER'], 'APCER': m['APCER'], 'BPCER': m['BPCER'],
        'AUC': m['AUC'], 'TDR': tdr, 'threshold': float(best_thresh),
        'best_dev_acer': float(best_dev_acer), 'n_real': n_real, 'n_fake': n_fake,
    })

print('\n' + '=' * 80)
print('All 6 folds trained. Run the summary / aggregation cell next.')
h, rem = divmod(int(time.time() - overall_start), 3600); mnt, s = divmod(rem, 60)
print(f'Total Protocol 3 time = {h:02d}:{mnt:02d}:{s:02d}')

from Functions.run_epochs_17 import *
from Functions.data_pipeline_setup_7 import *
from Functions.full_model_pipeline_13 import *
from Functions.loss_functions_14 import *
from Functions.optimiser_and_scheduler_15 import *

# ============================================================================
#  PROTOCOL 3 — Self-contained re-evaluation + summary (NO training)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Rebuilds the 6 folds' splits (inline loop), loads each saved checkpoint,
#  re-evaluates on that fold's Dev (threshold tuning) + Test (final metrics),
#  then produces the per-fold table, mean +/- std, JSON, text, and bar chart.
#
#  Requires already in memory: df, CFG, DEVICE, PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU,
#  REAL_DIR_OULU, CACHE_DIR_OULU, dev_transforms.
#  Requires on disk: the 6 checkpoints  <ckpt_prefix>fold1.pth .. fold6.pth
# ============================================================================

pcfg = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[3]
result_dir = pcfg['result']
result_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# --- Partition-file reader (OULU "label,video_name" -> video_name) ----------
def _read_ids(p):
    ids = set()
    with open(p) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            ids.add(line.split(',')[1].strip() if ',' in line else line)
    return ids

protocol3_fold_results = []

# ============================================================================
#  LOOP over the 6 folds: rebuild split -> load checkpoint -> evaluate
# ============================================================================
for fold in range(6):
    pos = fold + 1
    ckpt_path = Path(str(pcfg['ckpt_prefix']) + f'fold{pos}.pth')   # lowercase 'fold'

    if not ckpt_path.exists():
        print(f'[WARNING] Missing checkpoint for fold {pos}: {ckpt_path} — skipping.')
        continue

    print(f'Fold {pos}: rebuilding split + loading {ckpt_path.name} ...')

    # ---- Rebuild THIS fold's dev/test dataframes from partition files ------
    dev_ids  = _read_ids(pcfg['dev_P3'][fold])
    test_ids = _read_ids(pcfg['test_P3'][fold])
    dev_df   = df[df['subject_id'].isin(dev_ids)].copy()
    test_df  = df[df['subject_id'].isin(test_ids)].copy()

    # ---- Dev/test loaders (no training) ------------------------------------
    dev_dataset = PADVideoDataset(
        dev_df, real_dir=REAL_DIR_OULU, cache_dir=CACHE_DIR_OULU,
        transform=dev_transforms, demo_mode=False,
        use_freq=CFG.USE_FREQ_STREAM, use_flow=CFG.USE_FLOW_STREAM)
    test_dataset = PADVideoDataset(
        test_df, real_dir=REAL_DIR_OULU, cache_dir=CACHE_DIR_OULU,
        transform=dev_transforms, demo_mode=False,
        use_freq=CFG.USE_FREQ_STREAM, use_flow=CFG.USE_FLOW_STREAM)
    dev_loader = DataLoader(dev_dataset, batch_size=CFG.BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False,
                            num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, prefetch_factor=2, persistent_workers=True)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=CFG.BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False,
                             num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, prefetch_factor=2, persistent_workers=True)

    # ---- Load saved weights ------------------------------------------------
    model = HybridPADModel().to(DEVICE)
    ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=DEVICE, weights_only=False)
    model.load_state_dict(ckpt['state_dict'])
    criterion = CompoundFASLoss()

    # ---- Dev pass -> threshold minimising ACER -----------------------------
    _, _, dev_probs, dev_labels, _, _ = run_epoch(
        model, dev_loader, None, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)
    dev_labels_int = dev_labels.round().astype(int)
    thresholds = np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, 100)
    dev_acers = [compute_pad_metrics(dev_labels_int, dev_probs, t)['ACER'] for t in thresholds]
    best_thresh = thresholds[np.argmin(dev_acers)]

    # ---- Test pass -> final metrics at the Dev-tuned threshold -------------
    _, _, test_probs, test_labels, _, _ = run_epoch(
        model, test_loader, None, criterion, DEVICE, scaler=None, is_train=False)
    test_labels_int = test_labels.round().astype(int)
    m = compute_pad_metrics(test_labels_int, test_probs, threshold=best_thresh)
    tdr = compute_tdr_at_fdr(test_labels_int, test_probs, target_fdr=0.01)

    n_real = int((test_df['label'] == 0).sum())
    n_fake = int((test_df['label'] == 1).sum())

    print(f'  Fold {pos}: ACER {m["ACER"]*100:.2f}% | APCER {m["APCER"]*100:.2f}% | '
          f'BPCER {m["BPCER"]*100:.2f}% | AUC {m["AUC"]*100:.2f}% | TDR@1% {tdr:.2f}% '
          f'| thr {best_thresh:.3f}')

    protocol3_fold_results.append({
        'fold': pos, 'ACER': m['ACER'], 'APCER': m['APCER'], 'BPCER': m['BPCER'],
        'AUC': m['AUC'], 'TDR': tdr, 'threshold': float(best_thresh),
        'n_real': n_real, 'n_fake': n_fake,
    })

# ============================================================================
#  SUMMARY  (guarded so it won't nan-out if nothing loaded)
# ============================================================================
res = protocol3_fold_results
if not res:
    print('\n[ERROR] No checkpoints were evaluated — check the ckpt filename pattern.')
else:
    acer  = np.array([r['ACER']  for r in res]) * 100
    apcer = np.array([r['APCER'] for r in res]) * 100
    bpcer = np.array([r['BPCER'] for r in res]) * 100
    auc   = np.array([r['AUC']   for r in res]) * 100
    tdr   = np.array([r['TDR']   for r in res])

    lines = []
    lines.append('=' * 72)
    lines.append('PROTOCOL 3 — Leave-One-Camera-Out : per-fold results')
    lines.append('=' * 72)
    lines.append(f"{'Fold':<8}{'ACER%':>9}{'APCER%':>9}{'BPCER%':>9}{'AUC%':>9}{'TDR@1%':>9}")
    lines.append('-' * 53)
    for r in res:
        lines.append(f"{r['fold']:<8}{r['ACER']*100:>9.2f}{r['APCER']*100:>9.2f}"
                     f"{r['BPCER']*100:>9.2f}{r['AUC']*100:>9.2f}{r['TDR']:>9.2f}")
    lines.append('-' * 53)
    lines.append(f"{'MEAN':<8}{acer.mean():>9.2f}{apcer.mean():>9.2f}{bpcer.mean():>9.2f}{auc.mean():>9.2f}{tdr.mean():>9.2f}")
    lines.append(f"{'STD':<8}{acer.std():>9.2f}{apcer.std():>9.2f}{bpcer.std():>9.2f}{auc.std():>9.2f}{tdr.std():>9.2f}")
    lines.append('')
    lines.append(f"Headline (LOCO): ACER {acer.mean():.2f}% +/- {acer.std():.2f}  |  "
                 f"TDR@1% {tdr.mean():.2f}% +/- {tdr.std():.2f}")

    print('\n'.join(lines))

    with open(result_dir / 'summary_table_protocol_3.txt', 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines))
    print(f"\nSaved readable summary table to {result_dir / 'summary_table_protocol_3.txt'}")

    summary = {
        'protocol': 3, 'per_fold': res,
        'mean': {'ACER': float(acer.mean()), 'APCER': float(apcer.mean()),
                 'BPCER': float(bpcer.mean()), 'AUC': float(auc.mean()), 'TDR': float(tdr.mean())},
        'std':  {'ACER': float(acer.std()), 'APCER': float(apcer.std()),
                 'BPCER': float(bpcer.std()), 'AUC': float(auc.std()), 'TDR': float(tdr.std())},
    }
    with open(result_dir / 'test_metrics_protocol_3.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Saved summary to {result_dir / 'test_metrics_protocol_3.json'}")

    # ---- Per-fold bar chart ----
    labels = [f"Fold {r['fold']}" for r in res]
    x = np.arange(len(labels)); w = 0.38
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
    ax.bar(x - w/2, acer,  w, label='ACER',  color='#e76f51')
    ax.bar(x + w/2, apcer, w, label='APCER (spoof passed)', color='#2a9d8f')
    ax.axhline(acer.mean(), color='#e76f51', ls='--', lw=1.5, alpha=0.8,
               label=f'Mean ACER = {acer.mean():.2f}% +/- {acer.std():.2f}')
    for xi, v in zip(x - w/2, acer):
        ax.text(xi, v, f'{v:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
    for xi, v in zip(x + w/2, apcer):
        ax.text(xi, v, f'{v:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
    ax.set_title('Protocol 3 — Per-Fold Error (Leave-One-Camera-Out)', fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_ylabel('Error (%)'); ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
    ax.legend(); ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(result_dir / 'per_fold_barchart_protocol_3.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()
    print(f"Saved bar chart to {result_dir / 'per_fold_barchart_protocol_3.png'}")

# ============================================================================
#  PROTOCOL 4  —  All previous unseen scenarios combined   [OULU-NPU]
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Six camera folds. For each fold i (1..6): Train_i / Dev_i / Test_i hold the
#  videos for that fold's train / validation / test. A separate model is trained
#  per fold and results are averaged (mean +/- std) across the 6 folds.
#
#  This cell only BUILDS and VERIFIES the six folds (no training). Each fold's
#  train / dev / test dataframes are stored in lists for the training loop.
# ============================================================================
from Functions.config import *

# --- 1. Reader for the official partition files -----------------------------
#     OULU-NPU lines are "label,video_name" (e.g. "+1,4_1_11_4"); take the part
#     after the comma. set() de-duplicates any repeated names.
def _read_ids(p):
    ids = set()
    with open(p) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            if ',' in line:
                name = line.split(',')[1].strip()   # video name after the label
            else:
                name = line
            ids.add(name)
    return ids

pc = PROTOCOL_CONFIG_OULU[4]

# --- 2. Build + verify the six folds ----------------------------------------
train_dfs_P4 = []   # 6 train dataframes  (index 0 -> Fold 1, ... , index 5 -> Fold 6)
dev_dfs_P4   = []   # 6 dev/val dataframes
test_dfs_P4  = []   # 6 test dataframes

for fold in range(6):                                  # list index 0..5 (Fold 1..6)
    position = fold + 1                                     # human-readable fold/position number

    # Read this fold's three partition files
    train_ids = _read_ids(pc['train_P4'][fold])
    dev_ids   = _read_ids(pc['dev_P4'][fold])
    test_ids  = _read_ids(pc['test_P4'][fold])

    # Select the matching videos from df
    train_df = df[df['subject_id'].isin(train_ids)].copy()
    dev_df   = df[df['subject_id'].isin(dev_ids)].copy()
    test_df  = df[df['subject_id'].isin(test_ids)].copy()

    # Store for the training loop
    train_dfs_P4.append(train_df)
    dev_dfs_P4.append(dev_df)
    test_dfs_P4.append(test_df)

    # ---- Match check (this fold) ----
    print(f'\nMatch check (Fold {position}):')
    print(f'  Total no of train-files in the protocol = {len(train_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(train_df):>5}')
    print(f'  Total no of dev-files in the protocol = {len(dev_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(dev_df):>5}')
    print(f'  Total no of test-files in the protocol = {len(test_ids):>4} | Total no of videos that actually matched those names = {len(test_df):>5}')

    # Warn if any split matched nothing
    if len(train_df) == 0 or len(dev_df) == 0 or len(test_df) == 0:
        print('  !! WARNING: 0 matched — the split-file names do not match df["subject_id"].')
        print('     Example df stems:', df['subject_id'].head(3).tolist())
        print('     Example file ids :', list(train_ids)[:3])

    # ---- Totals ----
    print(f'\nFold {position}  ->  Train: {len(train_df):,} | Val: {len(dev_df):,} | Test: {len(test_df):,}')

    # ---- Per-class counts ----
    print(f'\nFold {position} Per-class counts:')
    for name, d in [('Train', train_df), ('Dev/Val', dev_df), ('Test', test_df)]:
        n_real = (d['label'] == 0).sum()
        n_fake = (d['label'] == 1).sum()
        print(f'  {name:<5}: real {n_real:>4} | fake {n_fake:>4}')

    print()   # blank line between folds

# --- 1. What's missing ---

missing_test  = test_ids_P4_F6  - set(df['subject_id'])

# --- 2. Show examples side by side: file names vs df names ---
print("Sample names IN THE PROTOCOL FILE (missing from df):")
print("  ", sorted(missing_test)[:10])
print("\nSample names IN df (subject_id):")
print("  ", sorted(set(df['subject_id']))[:10])

# --- 3. Format comparison — are they the same STYLE? ---
if missing_test:
    example_missing = sorted(missing_test)[0]
    example_df      = sorted(set(df['subject_id']))[0]
    print(f"\nFormat check:")
    print(f"  Missing file name : '{example_missing}'  (len={len(example_missing)})")
    print(f"  df subject_id     : '{example_df}'  (len={len(example_df)})")
    # Check for common mismatch causes
    print(f"  Missing has spaces? {' ' in example_missing}")
    print(f"  Missing has comma?  {',' in example_missing}")   # leftover label prefix?
    print(f"  Missing lowercase?  {example_missing.islower()}")

# --- 4. Is it a genuine missing FILE? Check if the video exists on disk ---
# Adjust the search root to where your OULU videos live
print("\nChecking if missing videos exist on disk:")
for name in sorted(missing_test)[:5]:
    # search for any file matching this name in your data root
    matches = list(REAL_DIR_OULU.parent.rglob(f"*{name}*"))   # adjust root as needed
    if matches:
        print(f"  '{name}' → FOUND on disk: {matches[0].name}  (so it's a MATCHING/format issue)")
    else:
        print(f"  '{name}' → NOT found on disk (genuinely missing video)")

# --- 5. Near-match check: is there a df name that's CLOSE to a missing one? ---
print("\nNear-match check (df names containing the missing name or vice versa):")
df_ids = set(df['subject_id'])
for name in sorted(missing_test)[:5]:
    near = [d for d in df_ids if name in d or d in name]
    print(f"  '{name}' → near matches in df: {near[:3] if near else 'NONE'}")

# ============================================================================
# CHECK 1 (Protocol 4) — Subject disjointness across train / dev / test
#                        for ALL 6 camera folds
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Goal: confirm NO subject appears in more than one split within each fold.
# ============================================================================

for fold in range(6):                          # list index 0..5  (Fold 1..6)
    position = fold + 1

    # Per-fold dataframes (from the split cell's lists), named for clarity
    train_df_P4_F = train_dfs_P4[fold]
    dev_df_P4_F   = dev_dfs_P4[fold]
    test_df_P4_F  = test_dfs_P4[fold]

    print('=' * 60)
    print(f'CHECK 1 — Subject disjointness across splits  (Fold {position})')
    print('=' * 60)

    # Unique subject sets per split
    train_subj_P4_F = set(train_df_P4_F['subject_id'])
    dev_subj_P4_F   = set(dev_df_P4_F['subject_id'])
    test_subj_P4_F  = set(test_df_P4_F['subject_id'])

    print(f'Unique subjects -> Train: {len(train_subj_P4_F)} | '
          f'Dev/Val: {len(dev_subj_P4_F)} | Test: {len(test_subj_P4_F)}')

    # Pairwise overlaps (each MUST be empty for no leakage)
    tv = train_subj_P4_F & dev_subj_P4_F
    tt = train_subj_P4_F & test_subj_P4_F
    vt = dev_subj_P4_F   & test_subj_P4_F

    print(f'\nOverlap Train ∩ Dev  : {len(tv)} subjects')
    print(f'Overlap Train ∩ Test : {len(tt)} subjects')
    print(f'Overlap Dev   ∩ Test : {len(vt)} subjects')

    if len(tv) == 0 and len(tt) == 0 and len(vt) == 0:
        print('\nPASS — all three splits are subject-disjoint (no leakage).')
    else:
        print('\nFAIL — subjects shared across splits (LEAKAGE):')
        if tv: print('   Train∩Dev :', list(tv)[:10])
        if tt: print('   Train∩Test:', list(tt)[:10])
        if vt: print('   Dev∩Test  :', list(vt)[:10])

    # Videos vs unique subjects per split (multiple videos per subject is fine)
    print('\nVideos vs unique subjects per split:')
    for name, d in [('Train', train_df_P4_F), ('Dev/Val', dev_df_P4_F), ('Test', test_df_P4_F)]:
        print(f'  {name:<5}: {len(d):>4} videos | {d["subject_id"].nunique():>4} unique subjects')

    print()   # blank line between folds

# ============================================================================
#  CACHE COVERAGE CHECK (Protocol 4)  —  directories, FFT files, flow files
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Protocol 3 has 6 camera folds, each with its own train/dev/test. Rather than
#  check one split, this gathers EVERY unique video used across all 6 folds
#  (train + dev + test) and verifies three levels of cache completeness:
#     1. the precompute DIRECTORY exists
#     2. all N_FRAMES  freq_*.npy  (FFT) files are present
#     3. all N_FRAMES  flow_*.npy  (optical flow) files are present
#  Any video failing a level triggers the on-the-fly recompute fallback in the
#  dataset (slower, and — for FFT — the source of the CUDA-in-worker crash),
#  so the goal is zero incompletes on every level.
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds (train+dev+test) ------
#     A video can appear in several folds; use a set of paths to check each once.
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P4[fold], dev_dfs_P4[fold], test_dfs_P4[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

missing_dir  = []   # videos with NO precompute folder at all
missing_fft  = []   # videos whose folder exists but freq_*.npy files are incomplete
missing_flow = []   # videos whose folder exists but flow_*.npy files are incomplete

for path in all_paths:
    vid_id  = Path(path).stem
    vid_dir = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id

    # ---- Level 1: does the cache directory exist at all? ----
    if not vid_dir.exists():
        missing_dir.append(vid_id)
        continue                       # no folder -> can't check files inside

    # ---- Level 2: count the FFT (freq) files inside the folder ----
    fft_files = list(vid_dir.glob('freq_*.npy'))
    if len(fft_files) < CFG.N_FRAMES:  # expect one freq file per frame
        missing_fft.append((vid_id, len(fft_files)))

    # ---- Level 3: count the optical-flow files inside the folder ----
    flow_files = list(vid_dir.glob('flow_*.npy'))
    if len(flow_files) < CFG.N_FRAMES: # expect one flow file per frame
        missing_flow.append((vid_id, len(flow_files)))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Report
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
total = len(all_paths)
print(f"Total unique videos (all 6 folds): {total}")
print(f"Missing cache directory          : {len(missing_dir)}")
print(f"Incomplete FFT (freq_*.npy)      : {len(missing_fft)}")
print(f"Incomplete flow (flow_*.npy)     : {len(missing_flow)}")

# Show a few examples for each problem level (only if any exist)
if missing_dir:
    print("\nExamples — missing directory:")
    print("  ", missing_dir[:10])
if missing_fft:
    print("\nExamples — incomplete FFT (vid_id, n_freq_files):")
    print("  ", missing_fft[:10])
if missing_flow:
    print("\nExamples — incomplete flow (vid_id, n_flow_files):")
    print("  ", missing_flow[:10])

# Clean bill of health
if not (missing_dir or missing_fft or missing_flow):
    print("\nAll cache directories, FFT files, and flow files are complete.")

Incomplete FFT (freq_*.npy)      : 0
Incomplete flow (flow_*.npy)     : 0

# ============================================================================
#  USABLE-FRACTION DISTRIBUTION (Protocol 4)  —  all videos across 6 folds
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Reads usable_frac from each video's cached video_meta.json and plots the
#  distribution. Videos below CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC were letterboxed (fallback);
#  the rest were properly aligned. Covers every unique video used across the
#  6 camera folds (train + dev + test).
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds -----------------------
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P4[fold], dev_dfs_P4[fold], test_dfs_P4[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

# --- Build the list of usable_frac values from cached video_meta.json --------
fracs = []
for path in all_paths:
    vid_id = Path(path).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        fracs.append(json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac'])

print(f"Collected usable_frac for {len(fracs)} / {len(all_paths)} videos")

# --- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.hist(fracs, bins=20, color='#534AB7', edgecolor='white')
ax.set_title('Distribution of usable landmark fraction per video (Protocol 4, all folds)',
             fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('usable_frac  (fraction of frames with good landmarks)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of videos', fontsize=11)

# Reference line at the align threshold
ax.axvline(CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC, color='orangered', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Align threshold ({CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC})')

# Region annotations
ax.text(0.97, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.9, 'Aligned\n(high quality)',
        ha='right', color='#1D9E75', fontsize=10)
ax.text(0.03, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.15, 'Letterbox\nfallback',
        ha='left', color='#D85A30', fontsize=10)

ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# --- Quick numeric summary ---------------------------------------------------
import numpy as np
fr = np.array(fracs)
below = (fr < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC).sum()
print(f"Below align threshold ({CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC}): {below} videos "
      f"({below / len(fr) * 100:.2f}%)")
print(f"Min {fr.min():.3f} | Median {np.median(fr):.3f} | Mean {fr.mean():.3f} | Max {fr.max():.3f}")

# ============================================================================
#  LETTERBOX CHECK (Protocol 4)  —  videos below the align threshold
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Collects videos whose usable_frac < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC (i.e. letterboxed
#  fallback), together with their attack types, across all 6 camera folds
#  (train + dev + test, each unique video counted once).
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique (path, label, attack_type) across all 6 folds -------
#     Deduplicate by path so a video shared across folds is checked once.
seen_paths = set()
records = []
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P4[fold], dev_dfs_P4[fold], test_dfs_P4[fold]):
        for _, row in d.iterrows():
            if row['path'] in seen_paths:
                continue
            seen_paths.add(row['path'])
            records.append(row)

# --- Collect videos below the align threshold, WITH their attack types -------
low_videos = []
for row in records:
    vid_id = Path(row['path']).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        uf = json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac']
        if uf < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC:          # < 0.70 -> letterboxed
            low_videos.append({
                'vid_id': vid_id,
                'label': row['label'],
                'attack_type': row.get('attack_type', 'unknown'),
                'usable_frac': round(uf, 3),
            })

print(f"Total letterboxed (usable_frac < {CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC}): {len(low_videos)}\n")

# Percentage of total (unique) videos that were letterboxed
total = len(records)
pct = (len(low_videos) / total * 100) if total else 0.0
print(f"Total unique videos (all 6 folds): {total}")
print(f"Letterboxed %                    : {pct:.6f}%")

# Only print the breakdowns if there ARE letterboxed videos
if low_videos:
    # Count per attack type
    attack_counts = Counter(v['attack_type'] for v in low_videos)
    print("\nLetterboxed videos by attack type:")
    for atk, cnt in attack_counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {atk:30s} : {cnt}")

    # Real vs fake split
    label_counts = Counter(v['label'] for v in low_videos)
    print(f"\nBy label: {dict(label_counts)}")

    # Full list
    print("\nIndividual videos:")
    for v in low_videos:
        print(f"  {v['vid_id']:25s} label={v['label']} attack={v['attack_type']:20s} uf={v['usable_frac']}")
else:
    print("\nNo letterboxed videos — all videos met the alignment threshold.")

# ============================================================================
#  META-FILE DIAGNOSTIC (Protocol 4)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Confirms the letterbox check is actually reading files (not silently finding
#  nothing). Checks two things across all 6 camera folds:
#    (1) how many video_meta.json files were actually found  (key diagnostic)
#    (2) how many of those are letterboxed (usable_frac < threshold)
#  If 'found' is far below the total, the cache path is wrong or precompute is
#  incomplete — and any "0 letterboxed" result would be meaningless.
# ============================================================================

# --- Gather every unique video path across all 6 folds -----------------------
all_paths = set()
for fold in range(6):
    for d in (train_dfs_P4[fold], dev_dfs_P4[fold], test_dfs_P4[fold]):
        all_paths.update(d['path'].tolist())

found = 0
low_videos = []
for path in all_paths:
    vid_id = Path(path).stem
    mp = CACHE_DIR_OULU / "precompute" / vid_id / "video_meta.json"
    if mp.exists():
        found += 1                              # count files actually found
        uf = json.load(open(mp))['usable_frac']
        if uf < CFG.ALIGN_MIN_FRAC:
            low_videos.append(vid_id)

print(f"Meta files found: {found} / {len(all_paths)}")   # the key diagnostic
print(f"Letterboxed: {len(low_videos)}")
